ma-g9-social-studies-u01.title: Foundations of High School United States History and Geography
ma-g9-social-studies-u01.rationale: Founding records let learners test provenance, constitutional structure, and competing historical claims.

ma-g9-social-studies-u02.title: Industrial and Urban America, 1870-1900
ma-g9-social-studies-u02.rationale: Federal policy and an industrial city image support claims about industrial growth, regulation, and uneven effects.

ma-g9-social-studies-u03.title: Becoming a World Power and World War I
ma-g9-social-studies-u03.rationale: A treaty, congressional proceedings, and an earlier foreign-policy statement support comparison of war aims and postwar choices.

ma-g9-social-studies-u04.title: The Progressive Era
ma-g9-social-studies-u04.rationale: Voting-rights, reform-organizing, and regulatory records support evaluation of Progressive-era institutional change.

ma-g9-social-studies-u05.title: Boom, Depression, and the New Deal
ma-g9-social-studies-u05.rationale: A New Deal statute, a period photograph, and an economic series support policy and evidence comparison.

ma-g9-social-studies-u06.title: World War II
ma-g9-social-studies-u06.rationale: An executive order, a judicial decision, and a later federal commission report provide primary and retrospective evidence about wartime incarceration.

ma-g9-social-studies-u07.title: Cold War and Postwar America
ma-g9-social-studies-u07.rationale: Foreign-policy, national-security, and veterans-policy records support claims about postwar institutions and opportunity.

ma-g9-social-studies-u08.title: Civil Rights in the Post-World War II Era
ma-g9-social-studies-u08.rationale: Court and statutory records support comparison of civil-rights claims, enforcement, and changing legal protections.

ma-g9-social-studies-u09.title: America in a New Global Age
ma-g9-social-studies-u09.rationale: Official demographic, economic, and trade data support measured claims about recent national and global change.

ma-g10-social-studies-u01.title: Foundations of World Historical and Geographical Inquiry
ma-g10-social-studies-u01.rationale: Historical maps and official statistics allow learners to compare scale, provenance, representation, and inference.

ma-g10-social-studies-u02.title: Hemispheric Interactions: World Religions and Trade Networks, 300-1500 CE
ma-g10-social-studies-u02.rationale: Map and museum records support cautious claims about exchange networks, religious material culture, and repository limits.

ma-g10-social-studies-u03.title: Dar al-Islam, the Mongols, and the Americas
ma-g10-social-studies-u03.rationale: Museum object records from different regions support comparison while requiring attention to date, place, and collection context.

ma-g10-social-studies-u04.title: The Emergence of the First Global Age
ma-g10-social-studies-u04.rationale: A world map, a voyage letter, and a coastal description support source criticism of early global connections and European perspectives.

ma-g10-social-studies-u05.title: Cultural Encounters, the Columbian Exchange, and the Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade
ma-g10-social-studies-u05.rationale: A published life narrative, a ship diagram, and a voyage letter support corroboration across different positions and source forms.

ma-g10-social-studies-u06.title: Global Revolutions, Migration, and Interconnection
ma-g10-social-studies-u06.rationale: Declarations of rights and a migration restriction record support comparison of revolutionary ideals, inclusion, and exclusion.

ma-g10-social-studies-u07.title: Nationalism, Industrialization, and Imperialism Compared
ma-g10-social-studies-u07.rationale: Industrial and cartographic records support comparison of production, territory, representation, and imperial viewpoints.

ma-g10-social-studies-u08.title: Global Crisis and Achievement, 1900-Present
ma-g10-social-studies-u08.rationale: Three official postwar international instruments support comparison of institutional purposes, rights claims, and enforcement limits.

ma-g10-social-studies-u09.title: Contemporary Global Issues
ma-g10-social-studies-u09.rationale: An international agreement, official statistics, and the UN document catalog support current-issue research with traceable authority.

ma-g11-social-studies-u01.title: Philosophical Foundations of Civic Society and Government
ma-g11-social-studies-u01.rationale: Founding texts and a ratification essay support comparison of political principles, institutional design, and author perspective.

ma-g11-social-studies-u02.title: Founding and Development of American Government
ma-g11-social-studies-u02.rationale: Ratification, rights, and reform records support analysis of constitutional development and contested inclusion.

ma-g11-social-studies-u03.title: Structure and Function of Governments in the United States
ma-g11-social-studies-u03.rationale: Federal and state constitutions plus legislative proceedings support comparison of structure, powers, and institutional action.

ma-g11-social-studies-u04.title: Rights and Liberties in the United States
ma-g11-social-studies-u04.rationale: Constitutional, judicial, and statutory records support tracing how rights claims and enforcement changed.

ma-g11-social-studies-u05.title: The United States in World Affairs and Citizenship in Action
ma-g11-social-studies-u05.rationale: International, citizenship, rulemaking, and docket records support inquiry into formal institutions and public participation.

ma-g11-social-studies-u06.title: The Market Economy: Scarcity, Decisions, and Competition
ma-g11-social-studies-u06.rationale: Official price, production, and population data support evidence-based market analysis and limitations checks.

ma-g11-social-studies-u07.title: Prices, Markets, and the Role of Government
ma-g11-social-studies-u07.rationale: Price data, budget records, and regulatory notices support analysis of market outcomes and government choices.

ma-g11-social-studies-u08.title: The National Economy
ma-g11-social-studies-u08.rationale: National accounts, labor releases, and monetary-policy records support triangulated macroeconomic claims.

ma-g11-social-studies-u09.title: The International Economy and Personal Finance
ma-g11-social-studies-u09.rationale: Trade and international statistics plus federal consumer guidance support connections between global markets and household decisions.

ma-g12-social-studies-u01.title: Research Design and the Arc of Inquiry
ma-g12-social-studies-u01.rationale: An official inquiry standard, two archival research systems, and a stable primary record support question design, evidence planning, and reproducibility.

ma-g12-social-studies-u02.title: Historiography and Contested Interpretation
ma-g12-social-studies-u02.rationale: Bibliographic guidance, a retrospective report, and a primary judicial record support comparison of interpretation and evidence.

ma-g12-social-studies-u03.title: Advanced Source Criticism and Evidence Standards
ma-g12-social-studies-u03.rationale: Finding aids, research guides, and a primary-record series support provenance, citation, and corroboration practice.

ma-g12-social-studies-u04.title: Comparative Government and Constitutional Design
ma-g12-social-studies-u04.rationale: Federal, state, and international constitutional instruments support comparison of authority, rights, and institutional design.

ma-g12-social-studies-u05.title: Geospatial and Quantitative Analysis for Social Science
ma-g12-social-studies-u05.rationale: Official geographic, demographic, economic, and international data support reproducible quantitative and spatial analysis.

ma-g12-social-studies-u06.title: Applied Economics and Policy Analysis
ma-g12-social-studies-u06.rationale: Cost estimates, program evaluations, rules, and budget records support policy comparison across evidence types and institutional roles.

ma-g12-social-studies-u07.title: Scoping the Capstone Issue: Contemporary Global and National Investigation
ma-g12-social-studies-u07.rationale: International records, nonpartisan congressional analysis, and statistics support bounded issue selection and source triangulation.

ma-g12-social-studies-u08.title: Public Discourse, Deliberation, and Argument from Evidence
ma-g12-social-studies-u08.rationale: Hearing, proceeding, and public-comment records support analysis of public arguments without supplying the learner's argument.

ma-g12-social-studies-u09.title: Capstone: Independent Research, Civic Action, and Public Defense
ma-g12-social-studies-u09.rationale: Stable archival, nonpartisan analysis, and public-docket systems provide a static research path while the learner retains authorship of the issue dossier and civic argument.
